summary: Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from San Francisco State University and her M.A. and Ph.D. at UCLA under William R. LaFleur, later serving as professor at Princeton University (1990–2019).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed doctoral research under Julius Lipner and held an academic post at the University of Manchester, both attested in 2005.

Jacques André was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1935–1948). He held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot was a French scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot in 1908. He held appointments at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1919 and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

Jacques Gernet was a scholar of sinology and history. Educated at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE, he held major posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1955–1976), Paris Diderot University (~1970–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Paris-Sorbonne under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and the École du Louvre (1998–2008), and served as president of the Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Paris-Sorbonne and INALCO, completing his PhD under Denise Bernot. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and joined the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques May was a specialist in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his doctorate under Constantin Régamey (~1950–1957), was a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1962–1992), and served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and the EFEO (~1968–1981).

Jacques Scheuer is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Université catholique de Louvain, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and under Madeleine Biardeau. He served as professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1977–2007) and held a post at Centre Sèvres.

Jadunath Sarkar was an Indian historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. During his career, he held positions at Patna College (1899–1926), Ravenshaw College (1919–1923), and served as vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Jae-gwon Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at Ryukoku University in 2007 and subsequently held an academic post there.
Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indologist who served in the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, where his work is attested between 1924 and 1930, and as Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Cambridge and served as director of the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911).

Jagannath Upadhyaya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1985).

Jagdish Kashyap was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and Vidyalankara Pirivena. He taught at BHU (~1940–1951), directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973), and was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965).

Jaideva Singh was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Srikrishna Harihirlekar and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from CUNY Graduate Center, and held teaching posts at Brown University (attested 2013–2018), City College of New York, and NYU.

Jakob Steiner studied at the universities of Heidelberg (1818–1821) and Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and the University of Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Oxford and completed his PhD and Habilitation under Richard von Garbe at Tübingen. He was an extraordinary professor at Marburg (1925–1927) and held a chair at Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy Hugh Barrett, and UCLA under Robert Buswell, he held posts at Arizona State University (attested 2004) and McMaster University (attested 2010–2017).
